title: Second Congo War
summary: On 2 August 1998 a rebellion broke out against President Laurent-Desire Kabila of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Rwanda, which admitted in November that its troops were helping the rebels, Uganda, Angola, Zimbabwe and Namibia all became involved, and new rebel groups appeared. A ceasefire signed at Lusaka in July 1999 brought a UN mission, but fighting went on. Kabila was assassinated in 2001, and a transitional government took office in 2003. The US State Department counts upwards of five million Congolese deaths.

uncertainty.note: Hostilities began on 2 August 1998 with mutinies against Kabila; major interstate warfare concluded with the installation of the transitional government in mid-2003.

beats.caption: Rebellion erupts against Laurent-Désiré Kabila in eastern Congo, quickly drawing in Rwandan and Ugandan military forces.
Regional belligerents sign the Lusaka Ceasefire Agreement, setting up the UN peacekeeping mission MONUC to monitor forces.
A power-sharing transitional government takes office in Kinshasa, ending large-scale interstate warfare that killed upwards of five million.
